This message comes from Capital One with the Capital One Saver Card.
Earn unlimited 3% cash back on dining and entertainment.
Capital One. What's in your wallet? Terms apply. Details at CapitalOne.com.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corova Coleman.
Tomorrow, the U.S. military formally pulls out of Iraq after more than two tumultuous decades there.
NPR's Jana Raff reports from Baghdad the withdrawal also marks the end of the anti-ISIS
coalition the U.S. has led since 2014. At what had been the Joint Military Command Center,
Iraqi workers are renovating. U.S. officers have operated from here since 2014, when Iraq asked
the U.S. military to return to fight the militant group ISIS. On Wednesday, U.S. commanders and
Iraqi leaders will mark the withdrawal of U.S. forces 23 years after the United States invaded Iraq.
Today, we are very proud to reach this day. That's Iraqi armed forces spokesman Sabah Al-Nouman.
At its height, during an eight-year-long occupation, the U.S. had 170,000
military personnel in Iraq. Jana Raff and Pure News beg dad.
The Trump administration banned about $1 billion worth of Canadian products overnight.
Dad Karpenzuk reports it's the latest escalation in the trade war between President Trump and the
Canadian government. The main items include some alcoholic beverages, dairy, and motorcycles.
President Trump's decision to go ahead with the ban will likely ratchet up trade tensions even
further, as the White House punishes Ottawa for retaliating earlier this month to previous
additional tariffs against Canada. Analysts say the ban isn't economically significant in the
nearly $1 trillion worth of trade between the two countries. Trump has already expressed confidence
that his latest moves would force Ottawa to come back to the negotiating table with an apology,
and a trade deal would come in three to four weeks. Canada has not indicated yet whether
there would be further retaliation, and the trade standoff could continue for months.
For NPR News, I'm Dan Karpenzuk in Toronto. Former Special Counsel Jack Smith is testifying
before the Senate Judiciary Committee about his past probes of President Trump. Some Republican
lawmakers want to see Smith criminally prosecuted. Smith says if he had the same set of facts
presented to him today, he would again choose to prosecute a president, regardless of party.
I stand by my testimony before the House of Representatives,
and I will not be silenced by continued threats of prosecution from the president or others.
Smith says the evidence that his investigative team gathered led to their decision to charge
President Trump. FBI Director Cash Patel says authorities in the Netherlands have arrested
a suspect alleged to be a member of a group of hackers. The group, called Shiny Hunters,
claimed to have stolen sensitive personnel data from the FBI. Writing online today, Patel thanked
the Dutch National Police for assisting in the arrest of the suspect. You're listening to NPR.
President Trump is announcing the relaunch of the website america.gov. It is supposed to use
AI tools to help people find federal information and resources spread across government services.
Trump will be joined later today by some AI industry leaders. The U.S. military says a Navy
jet crashed during landing on the carrier USS Dwight D. Eisenhower last night. It was off the
coast of Virginia Beach. From member station WHRO in Norfolk, Steve Walsh reports. According to the
Navy, the accident happened after 6 p.m. Eastern Time Monday. Two naval aviators from the third
carrier wing safely ejected and were recovered by the search and rescue personnel. They are being
evaluated. Four sailors on board USS Eisenhower were injured. One was flown to a Norfolk area
hospital for what the Navy describes as non-life-threatening injuries. The other three were
evaluated on board. Eisenhower is in training off the coast of Virginia as it gets ready for
deployment after coming out of a scheduled maintenance period in April. Eisenhower last
came home to Norfolk in July 2024 after nine months in the Middle East. The cause of the
accident is under investigation. For NPR News, I'm Steve Walsh. Forecasters have posted flood watches
from the desert southwest up to Iowa. There is a hurricane now hitting Mexico. This hurricane will
not hit the United States. But weather forecasters say the storm's tropical moisture will help create
heavy rainfall in the U.S. for the next several days. I'm Corfor Coleman, NPR News.
